 Kim visits China ahead of possible Trump summit

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un made a surprise visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Oct. 24, weeks before a regional summit in Shenzhen where he could meet U.S. President Donald Trump. The trip was Kim’s first to China in 13 months and his sixth since taking power. Analysts say he may be seeking to strengthen ties with Beijing and gain leverage in any future talks with Washington.
Kim crossed the New Yalu River Bridge into Dandong a day before the 76th anniversary of China’s entry into the Korean War, North Korea’s Korean Central News Agency and China’s Xinhua News Agency reported Oct. 25. He laid a wreath at the Monument to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea and toured its memorial hall. The name reflects Beijing’s official characterization of its intervention in the war.
At the memorial, Kim pledged to preserve the countries’ longstanding alliance. “We will forever remember the proud history of overcoming hardships together and carry forward the unbreakable friendship between North Korea and China, forged in blood,” he said. He also visited a bus manufacturing plant in Dandong before returning to North Korea that afternoon.
Wang Huning, China’s fourth-ranking Communist Party official and a close political and ideological adviser to President Xi Jinping, received Kim on Beijing’s behalf. Wang conveyed Xi’s greetings and proposed expanding people-to-people exchanges and economic cooperation following the opening of the New Yalu River Bridge. North Korean state media said Xi had personally ordered a welcoming banquet for Kim.
Li Qiang, China’s premier and second-ranking official, had also been mentioned as a possible host. A South Korean government official said Wang was likely chosen because he was better positioned to discuss broader political and bilateral issues, while Li focuses more on economic affairs.
The visit came ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, scheduled for Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend. Kim met Xi several times before and after his summits with Trump in 2018 and 2019. His latest trip has renewed speculation that he is drawing closer to Beijing to strengthen his hand in potential negotiations with Washington.
South Korea’s Presidential Office said Oct. 24 that it was closely monitoring developments surrounding Kim’s visit.
